findings.issue: Graded Documented, but no quoted line shows the act itself. Augustine reports a rumour: the followers of Pelagius 'are said to have' done it. Innocent's letter says the women 'left untold the name' of the attacker. Jerome's own account (Ep. 138) is in code names. Documented needs a quote that shows the relationship. These lines show a contemporary attribution, which is a different thing. The drafter flagged this, and the flag is right. The note itself is honest; only the grade overreaches.

findings.fix: Set confidence to 'Inferential-Thin' (keep citation_specificity 'A' and verification_state 'verified-direct'). By that bar the grade is one step too high. Continuity is the natural reading, but here it is an inference from two snapshots.

findings.issue: 'Continued as' means the same community carried into a later entry by a period split or rename. These two entries are not a split. They overlap from 451 to 589, and the Homoian entry has no continuesAs pointer. The Homoian text itself runs on to Toledo 589 and the Lombards. The drafter flagged the overlap. The sources show something else that the method already has a type for. Ulfila signed the Homoian creed of 360 as bishop of the Goths. The Goths took up that faith on the emperor's account. In 427 or 428 a Goth-escorted bishop still named that creed. That is a church that grew out of the imperial Homoian party: 'gave rise to'. It meets the Documented bar (named people passing, in a dated text). The Gothic entry's own summary reads the same way ('Descended from Ulfila's missionary church').

findings.issue: The prose pass turned the drafter's 'no direct line between the two has been traced' into 'though no one has traced a direct line between the two'. This states, as fact, a negative about all scholarship, and no source supports it. The drafter's reason was narrower: no vendored or repo-cited source supports descent.
